To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a sliding mode controller for linear uncertain systems with relative degree larger one, based on high gain observer, is presented.

the sliding mode controller (SMC) is a nonlinear control technique that has a number of advantages, including robustness, fast response, and the ability to handle nonlinearities, and that the proposed HGO-based SMC can achieve global exponential stability without generating the peaking phenomenon.
the proposed control law is a model-reference sliding mode control (MRSMC) law based on a high-gain observer (HGO).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a sliding mode controller for uncertain SISO linear systems.
sliding mode control of uncertain systems.
sliding mode control (SMC) of linear plants based on a high-gain observer (HGO).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HGO based controller has the following properties: i) it is a global controller, ii) it is free of the peaking phenomena, iii) the controller has a simple structure, iv) the controller is robust with respect to the uncertainty, and v) the controller is easy to implement.
the proposed control strategy provides an effective and efficient way of designing robust variable structure control systems with a high degree of performance and stability.
the proposed controller achieves global exponential stability for SISO linear plants with relative degrees greater than one and relative degree one with known high frequency gain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an HGO-based sliding mode control scheme which is free of peaking and has the ability to deal with the uncertainty.
we have proposed an alternative approach to the problem of sliding mode control of uncertain linear systems based on high gain observers.
we have developed a new model reference sliding mode control (SMC) scheme for SISO linear plants with relative degrees greater than one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a HGO can be used as a sliding mode observer for the purpose of generating a switching law.
the HGO can be used to generate switching signals in a model-reference sliding mode control scheme without the use of a high gain observer for state estimation and without the peaking phenomena.
a HGO can be used in a variable structure control scheme to achieve global stability with respect to the residual set without generating the peaking phenomenon.
